newsitem.title: USA: U.S. senators unveil campaign funds bill.
newsitem.headline: U.S. senators unveil campaign funds bill.

text.p: Five Democratic senators Tuesday unveiled a new campaign finance reform bill to try to diminish the role of "special interest money" in the political system.

The bill, sponsored by Sens. John Kerry of Massachusetts, Paul Wellstone of Minnesota, Joe Biden of Delaware, John Glenn of Ohio and Patrick Leahy of Vermont, would prohibit private contributions to political candidates who agreed to accept spending limits in exchange for public financing.

This would allow candidates to be free of the special interest groups on which many depend for campaign contributions and would give challengers a better chance to take on incumbents, the senators said.

The bill would also prohibit so-called "soft money" contributions to national parties. There are no limits on such contributions as long as they are not used specifically to promote any individual candidate.
Like other campaign reform bills, the legislation appeared to have little chance of going anywhere in the current Congress in the face of opposition from the Republican leadership.

But the senators said they hoped to build on a grassroots movement which has already succeeded in having similar proposals adopted in Maine and Vermont and was working on ballot measures in several other states.
"We are going to go out to the country ... to once again make politics accountable," said Kerry.
Wellstone said voters knew "there's been a hostile takeover of this electoral process and the governmental process by big money."
